# Jeremiah 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD gave this message to Jeremiah:

**2** "Listen to the terms of My covenant, and pass them on to the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

**3** Tell them that the LORD, the God of Israel, says: A curse falls on anyone who refuses to obey the terms of this covenant!

**4** These are the terms I gave your ancestors when I brought them out of Egypt, out of that iron furnace of suffering. I told them, 'If you obey Me and do whatever I command, then you will be My people, and I will be your God.'

**5** I said this so that I could keep the promise I made to your ancestors — to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, the land you live in today." I replied, "Yes, LORD, let it be so!"

**6** Then the LORD said, "Broadcast this message in the streets of Judah and Jerusalem: Listen to the terms of My covenant and carry them out!

**7** From the day I brought your ancestors out of Egypt until now, I have warned them again and again, saying, 'Obey My voice.'

**8** But they didn't listen or pay attention. Instead, each one followed the stubborn desires of their evil hearts. So I brought on them all the punishments described in this covenant — the covenant they agreed to but never kept."

**9** Then the LORD said to me, "I have discovered a conspiracy among the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

**10** They've gone back to the sins of their ancestors, who refused to listen to Me. They're chasing after other gods and serving them. Both Israel and Judah have broken the covenant I made with their ancestors."

**11** So the LORD says, "I am going to bring a disaster on them that they won't be able to escape. Even if they cry out to Me, I won't listen.

**12** Then the people of Judah and Jerusalem will run to their gods and beg for help — the very gods they've been burning incense to. But those gods won't be able to do a thing to save them when disaster strikes.

**13** You have as many gods as you have towns, Judah! And look at all those altars to Baal — one on every street corner in Jerusalem, altars built to your shame.

**14** Don't bother praying for these people, Jeremiah. Don't plead or beg on their behalf. I will not listen when they cry out to Me in their time of distress.

**15** What right do My beloved people have to come to My Temple when they've been doing so many evil things? Do they think animal sacrifices will save them from punishment? Do they think that will make them celebrate?

**16** I once called them 'My beautiful olive tree, loaded with fruit.' But now I have set it on fire with the roar of a mighty storm, and its branches are being destroyed.

**17** The LORD of Armies, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you. Why? Because both Israel and Judah have done evil and provoked Me to anger by offering sacrifices to Baal."

**18** Then the LORD told me about the plots my enemies were making against me.

**19** I had been as unsuspecting as a lamb being led to slaughter. I had no idea they were planning to kill me! They said, "Let's destroy this man and everything he says. Let's cut him off from the land of the living so that no one will even remember his name."

**20** But LORD of Armies, You are a righteous judge! You examine the deepest thoughts and secrets. Let me see You take revenge on these people, for I have committed my cause to You.

**21** So the LORD spoke about the men of my hometown, Anathoth, who wanted me dead. They told me, "Stop prophesying in the LORD's name, or we will kill you!"

**22** So the LORD of Armies says, "I will punish them! Their young men will die in battle. Their sons and daughters will starve to death.

**23** Not one of them will survive when I bring disaster on Anathoth — the year of their reckoning."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **11:4**: Egypt was an 'iron furnace' — not just slavery but a crucible. God's people were forged in suffering, which makes their betrayal all the more painful.

- **11:19**: This is one of the most haunting passages — Jeremiah was clueless about the murder plot. His own neighbors, his own family, wanted him dead for speaking God's truth.

- **11:14**: God tells Jeremiah to stop praying for the people. That's terrifying. When God says 'don't bother interceding,' it means the opportunity for repentance has passed.

— PNEUMA
